title: Week Ahead — Market Outlook
headline: Markets enter a data-heavy week with contained spot volatility but meaningful two-way risk from inflation prints, Treasury supply, earnings, options expiry and geopolitical oil shocks.
volatilityRationale: Spot volatility is still relatively contained, but the event stack is unusually dense: PPI, CPI, Treasury auctions, earnings and weekly options expiry arrive while Iran/Hormuz tensions continue to feed oil and rate risk. A data surprise that shifts expectations for the September Fed meeting could quickly reprice duration-sensitive equities.

recap.text: U.S. equities finished the shortened week nearly flat-to-positive: the S&P 500 rose 0.1% and Nasdaq 0.4%, while the Dow fell 0.3%, according to the weekly market recap.

Friday's hotter-than-expected August employment report, including 162,000 payroll additions, pushed Treasury yields higher and pressured stocks as traders reassessed the odds of a rate hike later this month.
The market narrative last week balanced the Fed path against renewed Iran-related oil risk; Nasdaq's weekly review also flagged Waller's patience signal and the earnings-season impact of Broadcom.

The Cboe page showed a 14.53 VIX close on September 4, while the latest Monday quote feed was 15.12; that is a low-to-mid-teens volatility backdrop, not a panic regime, but it leaves room for event-driven repricing.

triggers.text: U.S. Treasury supply: the tentative schedule lists a 3-year note auction on September 8 and a 10-year note auction on September 9, making duration demand and term-premium sensitivity important rate-market tests.
U.S. PPI, weekly jobless claims and existing-home sales are due, alongside an ECB decision; a hotter inflation or labor signal could reinforce the post-jobs hawkish repricing.
The August U.S. CPI report, preliminary University of Michigan sentiment and the Treasury Statement arrive together, concentrating inflation and consumer-expectations risk into Friday's open.
GameStop and ServiceTitan are scheduled to report after the Labor Day reopening, providing an early read on consumer and software-spending sentiment.
Oracle and Adobe are among the week's notable earnings reports, with software demand and AI monetization likely to be read through to the broader technology complex.
Weekly equity and ETF options expire Friday, adding potential dealer-flow and pinning effects into the same session as CPI and consumer-sentiment data.

watch.text: Fed repricing: compare CPI/PPI outcomes with the strong jobs signal and watch whether the market pulls forward expectations for the September 15–16 FOMC meeting.
Oil and geopolitical transmission: renewed Iran or Strait of Hormuz escalation could lift energy prices, inflation expectations and Treasury yields at the same time.
Treasury demand and rate-sensitive breadth: watch the 10-year auction, the 10-year yield and whether small caps continue to hold up as yields rise.
